answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the signal check immediately, the quill audit keeps the resolved set and the marble replay shows exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 56 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 56 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
